subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should this be fixed as a narrow safe read fallback, richer core document extraction, or deferred to broader document/file-input architecture?
rationale: The source-reproducible token-waste problem is real, but the chosen solution changes the core read-tool boundary and ranges from a small warning-only guard to security-sensitive document parsing or provider-native file forwarding.

options.title: Approve Narrow Read Fallback
options.body: Add a bounded PDF/Office MIME and extension guard in the current read path that returns a clear unsupported-document message and directs PDF users to the pdf tool.

options.title: Sponsor Native Extraction
options.body: Define parser ownership, dependencies, archive/XML limits, sandbox behavior, and tests before adding native DOCX/PPTX/XLSX extraction.

options.title: Defer To File-Input Work
options.body: Keep read unchanged for now and link this issue to the broader document extraction and provider-native file-input architecture trackers.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Read Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a bounded PDF/Office MIME and extension guard in the current read path that returns a clear unsupported-document message and directs PDF users to the pdf tool.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Office-path and read-wrapper work makes this the strongest available routing signal for the read boundary decision.
